html:
The Poteskeet were a small Algonquian people of the Currituck Sound area in northeastern North Carolina, on the mainland behind the Outer Banks. They are usually counted as part of the Weapemeoc, a people first noted by the English of the Roanoke colony in 1585 and 1586.

They fished and gathered in the sounds and farmed maize. Their neighbours included the Chowanoke and the Secotan. When the explorer John Lawson wrote about Carolina's peoples in 1709, he found only a few Poteskeet left. They disappear from records soon after.
